thread.title: Carriers' Deals on New iPhones Are Good News for Apple - Barron's - iWorld

title: Carriers' Deals on New iPhones Are Good News for Apple - Barron's - iWorld
text:
Photo: Courtesy of Apple By David Marino-Nachison Sept. 24, 2018 2:51 p.m. ET Attractive mobile carrier deals on Apple (AAPL) phones might be a sign that the latest iPhone releases could lead to “healthy” sales volumes.
That’s the take from RBC Capital Markets analysts, who on Sunday wrote that while the company could see earnings per share growth in the “low to mid teens” if iPhone unit sales are “flattish,” the newest lineup of phones could help drive “low-to-mid single digit growth this cycle.”
Their analysis follows Apple’s announcement of its newest phones : the iPhone XS, the oversize iPhone XS Max, and the on-the-way iPhone XR. (We recently gathered up reviewers’ impressions of the first two .) The phones arrive as Apple is evolving into a company that’s about selling services and boosting average phone prices — even if it can’t easily grow the phone sales themselves.
Newsletter Sign-up RBC said the latest round of iPhone promotions looks “more attractive” than they did last year: Verizon (VZ), for example, has an offer to buy one new iPhone and get $700 off another with a new line. There are also offers from Sprint (S), T-Mobile US (TMUS) and AT&T (T).
“A wide iPhone portfolio should have a wider appeal and help gain share vs. Android,” the RBC analysts wrote. “Further, users have little reason to delay their purchases now for a better phone lineup now that the average selling price uplift that accompanied iPhone X is likely to continue with every generation.”
The phones are new, but observers are already trying to figure out how the market is responding. On Monday, Rosenblatt Securities’ Jun Zhang wrote that the iPhone XS and the iPhone XS Max outsold the older iPhone X over the weekend.
But orders for the new phones are “very weak,” according to Zhang, and the X might outsell the others over the next two months. (Preorders for the less-expensive iPhone XR, however, may be stronger than for the other two phones, he wrote.)
Recommended Reading The Rest of Tech Leans Into Apple’s Shadow All Eyes Are on the Price of Apple’s New iPhones Apple’s iPhone Event Was a Snoozer. But Don’t Sleep on the Stock The newer phones may have in China, according to Morgan Stanley analysts. The phones’ new “dual sim” feature lets owners travel internationally more easily and thus makes the phones more competitive overseas. (More than half of all smartphones in the region have it, according to Morgan Stanley, but less than 5% in North America do.)
Another analyst reported that the iPhone XS Max, which has Apple’s largest screen, is outselling the smaller iPhone XS . And a McClatchy story visited stores in cities around the world, spotting lines that seemed “shorter than in previous years.”
Among the locations McClatchy visited: Syracuse, N.Y, where a reporter asked a shopper about the smallish crowd. “It’s Syracuse, not New York City,” the shopper replied.
